read_log.table_note: Each row records a user's reading progress event on a specific article within a session, including the initial page view and subsequent percentage-based read checkpoints (20% through 100%). This table is for analyzing article engagement depth and reading completion rates.

column_notes.note: The 'view' action marks the initial page load, while 'read-XX%' actions (20% through 100%) track scroll/reading progress. These percentage values are not found in any other table and represent a unique engagement tracking mechanism.
column_notes.unsupported: The 'view' action marks the initial page load
column_notes.fact: The read_log table contains action values including 'view' and 'read-XX%' (20% through 100%). The action_log, access_log, activity_log, and form_log tables contain zero records where the action column matches the pattern 'read%'.

column_notes.note: Sessions in this table do not appear in access_log or any other log table, suggesting these are isolated reading sessions or the session IDs are not shared across the logging system.
column_notes.unsupported: the session IDs are not shared across the logging system

column_notes.note: The URL contains an article ID parameter (e.g., id=news731). Analysts should extract this ID to join with product or content tables if available, but no such content table exists in this database.

column_notes.fact: The read_log table contains a url column with values like 'http://www.example.com/article?id=news341' that include an article ID parameter.

pitfalls.note: Since sessions in read_log are not linked to any other table (no user_id, no matching sessions in access_log), analysts cannot join this table to user demographics or purchase data without external data.
pitfalls.unsupported: no user_id, no matching sessions in access_log

pitfalls.note: The action column uses percentage strings like 'read-20%' which must be parsed (extracting the number) before computing average read depth or comparing across articles.

pitfalls.fact: The action column in the read_log table contains values such as 'view', 'read-20%', 'read-40%', 'read-60%', 'read-80%', and 'read-100%'.
